Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A March 2025 report indicated that U.S. uranium producers are planning for continued growth in 2025, following a production increase throughout 2024. [9] In the fourth quarter of 2024, production of uranium concentrate at U.S. facilities reached its highest level since the third quarter of 2018. [9] Producers are now awaiting clearer signals from Washington, D.C., regarding the impacts of tariffs, shifting relationships with global suppliers, and funding designed to increase demand for domestic uranium. [9] <2> U.S. Representative John McGuire of Virginia's 5th congressional district introduced the 'Uranium for Energy Independence Act of 2025'. [6] This legislation proposes adding uranium to the United States Geological Survey's (USGS) list of critical minerals. [6] <3> On February 4, 2025, Trading Economics published a forecast predicting that the price of uranium would reach $72.18 per pound by March 31, 2025, which marks the end of the first quarter of the year. <4> In January 2025, the uranium market experienced significant volatility, a development that analysts attributed to several factors, including the start of a second Trump administration. A report published on February 13, 2025, noted that uranium prices fell by 3.09% in January, finding support around $70 per pound. This turbulence was linked to the new administration's pro-nuclear stance, which aimed to reshape U.S. energy policy, and the introduction of trade measures and tariffs that created uncertainty for the sector. Another contributing factor cited was the emergence of the Chinese artificial intelligence model, DeepSeek. Despite the drop in spot prices, an outlook from Sprott on January 28, 2025, remained bullish on the long-term prospects, citing a steady increase in term market prices over the preceding 28 months, driven by reactor life extensions and new builds. The analysis highlighted a frustrating year for spot prices in 2024 but anticipated that pent-up demand would support prices moving forward. <5> In a statement on January 28, 2025, Sprott Asset Management's CEO, John Ciampaglia, expressed a bullish outlook for the uranium market. He anticipated that uranium prices would strengthen during the first quarter of 2025 as buyers returned to the market. Ciampaglia acknowledged a recent correction in the spot market, with the price ending the previous year around $76, but asserted that the long-term market fundamentals have grown stronger. <6> On January 28, 2025, a published analysis of the uranium market highlighted a bullish outlook for future prices despite a 30% decrease in contracting volumes in 2024. [6, 11] The term price for uranium continued to rise, a trend supported by utilities signing long-term contracts with floor prices of $79 and ceiling prices approaching $150 per pound. [11] This confidence in the market was attributed to a widening supply-demand imbalance, geopolitical reshaping of supply chains, and the increasing role of nuclear power in the global clean energy transition. [6] <7> The uranium market concluded 2024 with a spot price of $72.63 per pound and a long-term price of $80.50 per pound as of December 31, 2024. These figures are industry averages calculated by Cameco, a major global uranium provider, based on month-end prices from UxC and TradeTech. The spot price had decreased from a high of $100.25 in January 2024, while the long-term price has been on a gradual upward trend for several years.
